title: Re-routing keeps every contact persistent, but only lines read their distance plainly
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: Exchanging, at any set of contacts, which ring each arriving ring continues on keeps the contact graph and, at law-(12,12) contacts, the automaton itself, so every re-routing of a lattice torus keeps every contact persistent, and random ones have no flips. Grouped into lines the tori's automata read their distance plainly at every size; on the square contact graph no grouping into small rings does.
